articles.summary: December is almost here, and so is one of our favorite coding traditions! We’re excited to take part in Advent of Code once again and invite you to join us for another season of festive puzzles, clever Kotlin solutions, and friendly competition.

articles.title: GPT-6.2 Astra users now hit limits 40% faster after OpenAI patched a pricing error
articles.summary: OpenAI says a billing bug gave GPT-6.2 users incorrect discounts. After the fix, Astra and Sol users hit their limits 40 and 25 percent faster than last week.

articles.title: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
articles.summary: My comment on The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features — Hacker News. I had a NYT photographer take my picture at my home earlier this year (for a story about Moltbook, oddly enough).

articles.title: A Modular 6502 Computer
articles.summary: Back in the day, there were plenty of nice compact microcomputers out there that featured the 6502 CPU. There were also simpler computers that put the chip on a bare board and put you very closer to the bare metal.

articles.title: Compatibility tool manager ProtonPlus adds game support to Lutris, Faugus, Heroic Games, and Bottles
articles.summary: In version 0.6.9 that just went out - you can now manage games and their runners directly in the app for the likes of Lutris, Faugus Launcher, Heroic Games Launcher, and Bottles.

articles.title: When Decoupling Capacitors Go Wrong
articles.summary: Popular wisdom holds that decoupling capacitors are good, and thus more decoupling capacitors is better. Unfortunately physics disagrees on that notion, as [Ben Eater] discusses in a recent video , following feedback from a viewer who found that upon adding said capacitors, their supply rail got unstable and began oscillating.

articles.title: The Motorola Signature 27’s haptics finally feel more like a Pixel, and it’s about time
articles.summary: Typing on the Signature 27 is pure bliss because of it. Tapping each key feels more like the press of a physical keyboard key. Unlocking the phone emits a satisfying light punch to my thumb, signalling a successful read.

articles.title: VR mech game IRON REBELLION gets a big PvE campaign update on December 14
articles.summary: Coming as a free update for everyone, the awesome looking VR mech battler IRON REBELLION is getting a single-player PvE campaign. Currently it's only an online PvP game, which is not great for a niche like VR with so few players.

articles.title: What, Who, and When: Structured Harm Assessment for Mental Health Safety via Short Reasoning
articles.summary: The growing use of large language models (LLMs) for mental health support raises important safety concerns. Existing guard models primarily identify categories of harmful content, often overlooking the context needed to determine an appropriate response.

articles.title: Certify What You Plant: Shortcut-Free Proof Depth in Logical Reasoning Data
articles.summary: Procedurally generated logic problems are used to both evaluate and train reasoning in language models. Their difficulty is usually set by planting a proof, that is, by sampling a proof of the desired depth and stating its premises as the problem.

articles.title: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis in Jacobian-Space: Language and Vision Models Agree Approximately Up to a Rotation
articles.summary: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) posits that AI models converge toward a shared representation of the world, even when trained on different data modalities. Previous work has found evidence for the PRH in the activations of vision and language models.

articles.title: Brand Recall and Category Accuracy in Language Models: An Audit of 1,000 B2B SaaS Brands
articles.summary: A language model can name a brand without classifying it correctly. This study measures these outcomes separately for 1,000 B2B SaaS brands across 333 product categories.

articles.title: New Linux kernel patches unlock native resolution on 4K/5K iMacs
articles.summary: Owners of 4K and 5K iMacs could soon enjoy their screen’s full native resolution on Linux, thanks to a set of proposed kernel patches. I run Ubuntu on a 2017 21.5-inch iMac with a 4K display.

articles.title: Linux Mint 27 beta downloads are available for testing
articles.summary: Beta builds of Linux Mint 27 ‘Adrien’ have hit the distro’s official download mirrors, though there’s been no official announcement about it yet. Linux Mint 27 is built on Ubuntu 26.04 LTS and the Linux 7.0 kernel.

articles.title: It Looks Like AI Agent Skills Will Be Submitted For Linux 7.5
articles.summary: For the upcoming Linux 7.5 merge window happening in late December, it appears that AI agent skills will be submitted for adding in-tree documentation for instructing AI agents on different kernel processes.

articles.title: Ubuntu 27.04 Snapshot 1 Released For Testing
articles.summary: For those with extra time around the US Thanksgiving holiday, the first Tenacious Snapshot 1 was just released today as the first stepping stone toward Ubuntu 27.04.
